item.title: Active shooter report at Oregon elementary school draws large police response
item.description: Bend police responded to Silver Rail Elementary School after an active shooter report, directing families to a nearby church for reunification.
item.content:encoded:
Police rushed to an Oregon elementary school Thursday after a report of an active shooter, urging the public to stay away as families were directed to a nearby church.

The Bend Police Department said officers were at Silver Rail Elementary School, where a large police presence gathered as authorities responded.

"The Bend Police Department is currently at Silver Rail Elementary School after a report of an active shooter," the department said in a statement. "There is a large police presence in the area. Please avoid the area."

REPORTED SHOOTING AT VIRGINIA ELEMENTARY SCHOOL 'CONTAINED,' SHERIFF'S OFFICE SAYS

Authorities directed students’ families to Journey Church at 61303 S. Highway 97, near Goodwill and Dairy Queen, which was designated as the family reunification location.

Police had not immediately released information about injuries or a possible suspect. It was not immediately clear whether authorities had confirmed gunfire at the school.

"We will share more information as soon as we can," the department said.

This is a developing story. Check back for updates.

item.title: Guardians shut down Rays behind pitching staff, epic Petey Halpin bat-flip for Game 3 win to take series lead
item.description: Petey Halpin's towering 385-foot two-run homer powered the Cleveland Guardians past the Tampa Bay Rays after weather moved the Game 3 start to 1 p.m. ET.
item.content:encoded:
Game 3 was moved up from 6 p.m. ET to 1 p.m. ET due to weather, but the Tampa Bay Rays' offense did not get the memo.

In the team's 3-2 loss to the Cleveland Guardians on Thursday at Progressive Field, the offense was dormant. The Rays scored just two runs on three hits, as the Guardians' pitching staff shut them down. In seven of the nine innings, the Rays went down in order.

The 1 p.m. start was the earliest for an LCS game in the Eastern time zone since 1988, when the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets played Game 5 of the NLCS at 12:20 p.m. ET.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Guardians bats struck first off Griffin Jax. Jo Adell worked a walk (after successfully overturning a called strike with the automated ball-strike challenge system), and was driven in one batter later when Nathaniel Lowe ripped a ball into right field, taking a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the second inning.

Adell was able to score from first after the ball got away from right fielder Victor Mesa Jr., while Lowe advanced to second base. Jax was able to strand Lowe by recording the next three outs.

Gavin Williams was lights out to begin the game, retiring the Rays in order the first time through the lineup.

However, Rays first baseman Yandy Díaz broke through, ripping a leadoff double into the left-center gap for the team’s first baserunner of the game. Williams struck out Jonathan Aranda and Junior Caminero but walked Mesa to put two runners on with two outs.

The two-out walk came back to burn Williams. Chandler Simpson laced a line drive down the right-field line, scoring both Díaz and Mesa while the speedster raced to third for a triple, giving the Rays a 2-1 lead in the top of the fourth inning.

Williams was able to strand Simpson at third by striking out catcher Liam Hicks to end the frame.

The Guardians responded in the bottom of the fifth inning. Catcher Patrick Bailey hit a weak dribbler for an infield single to lead off the inning, and center fielder Petey Halpin deposited Jax’s pitch 385 feet over the right-center field wall for a two-run home run to give the Guardians a 3-2 lead.

His bat almost went as far as the ball, as Halpin launched his bat high into the Cleveland sky in celebration. After the game, Halpin said he blacked out and said the celebration may have even been a little too much.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Shortstop Bryan Rocchio singled after Halpin’s home run, and manager Kevin Cash had seen enough, pulling Jax from the game.

Jax pitched four-plus innings, giving up three runs on five hits while walking two batters and striking out two. Tyler Wells navigated the rest of the fifth inning to keep the score at 3-2.

Surprisingly, Guardians manager Stephen Vogt pulled Gavin Williams from the game after just 70 pitches in five innings, bringing in Daniel Espino. Williams pitched five innings, giving up two runs on two hits with two walks while striking out nine batters.

While it may have been surprising to see Williams removed, the bullpen was excellent. Espino and Erik Sabrowski made quick work of the Rays' lineup in the sixth and seventh innings. Hunter Gaddis entered the game in the eighth inning and recorded two outs but allowed a double to Richie Palacios.

Palacios advanced to third base on Taylor Walls' groundout, and Vogt turned to his closer, Cade Smith, to face Díaz in a crucial spot in the top of the eighth inning.

After a 10-pitch battle with Díaz, Smith struck out the Rays first baseman to escape the jam In the ninth inning, Smith faced Jonathan Aranda, Junior Caminero and Mesa, the Nos. 2, 3 and 4 hitters in the order, and retired them with ease, completing the four-out save. The Guardians pitching staff retired 16 of the last 17 batters.

Game 4 between the Guardians and Rays is scheduled for Friday, but inclement weather could delay or postpone the game. First pitch is scheduled for 6 p.m. ET.

item.title: Warriors rookie's reaction to learning he'd guard Lakers superstar Luka Dončić goes viral: 'What the f---?'
item.description: Yaxel Lendeborg revealed his stunned reaction when Frank Vogel told him he'd guard Luka Dončić in the Golden State Warriors' preseason game.
item.content:encoded:
A "Welcome to the NBA" moment almost occurred for Golden State Warriors top draft pick Yaxel Lendeborg on Tuesday night in a preseason bout against the Los Angeles Lakers.

He was supposed to guard Luka Dončić — an assignment many veteran defenders don’t wish to have, let alone a rookie.

Lendeborg, the No. 11 overall pick coming out of the national-champion Michigan Wolverines program, told reporters that he was just on his phone before the game when assistant Warriors coach Frank Vogel came up to him and said something that left him baffled.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"’Hey, you’re guarding Luka tonight,’" Lendeborg said. "I said, ‘What the f---? You’re just gonna throw me in the fire?’"

To be honest, not an over-exaggerative answer at all for a rookie trying to get acclimated to the league.

Lendeborg’s reaction was genuine because he didn’t think his assignment would be the Lakers’ star player and one of the most prolific offensive weapons in the league when he’s on the court.

Ultimately, Lakers head coach JJ Redick decided to rest Dončić, leading to Lendeborg matching up with center Walker Kessler, who debuted this preseason for Los Angeles. The Warriors ended up winning the game, 101-89.

LUKA DONČIĆ SAYS HE 'DEFINITELY' REGRETS PLAYING THROUGH HAMSTRING INJURY THAT ENDED HIS SEASON

"It was a complete shift of what I had planned in my mind," Lendeborg said about gearing up for the game before hearing the Dončić news.

Lendeborg is, however, a solid defender, winning Defensive Player of the Year in the AAC with UAB before becoming a first-team all-defense member in the Big Ten during his season at Michigan in 2025.

Guarding Dončić is completely different than going up against even the best college players, but Lendeborg tried his best to play the part.

"I tried to act all cool, but I was spooked," he admitted. "That was crazy."

"I think [Vogel] said he averages like 30, 35. Nobody can stop him, so do your best. That was it. My mind was all over the place after that."

No defender wants to be put through a clinic by his opponent, so it’s understandable how Lendeborg feels. But to Vogel’s point, Dončić is someone that can hit shots even with great defense, averaging 33.5 points per game last season, which led the NBA.

In the end, Lendeborg held his own against Kessler, while also dropping 19 points on the other end of the floor.

Looking ahead to the regular season, Lendeborg will likely be utilized by head coach Steve Kerr as a versatile defender, with the 6-foot-9 rookie able to handle multiple assignments, no matter his opponent’s position on the court.

So, while the matchup with Dončić didn’t come this time around, the Warriors and Lakers will tip off their regular season schedule on Oct. 21 in Los Angeles.

If that happens, well, best of luck, Yaxel. Welcome to the NBA.

item.title: Colin Cowherd's analogy of the 2026 Dodgers to The Godfather Part III is brilliant
item.description: Colin Cowherd compares the Los Angeles Dodgers' stunning 0-3 postseason hole to "The Godfather Part III" — familiar names, but fading magic.
item.content:encoded:
Perhaps the best analogy for the stunning 0-3 hole the Los Angeles Dodgers find themselves in comes from The Godfather – the third installment of the trilogy, that is.

Credit FS1 host Colin Cowherd for the comparison Wednesday.

"The Dodgers trying to win a third World Series is starting to have Godfather III vibes to it," he began. "Some of the names are familiar. Al Pacino. Diane Keaton. Francis Ford Coppola is still directing it. But it feels played. And the Dodgers feel played out."

Brilliant.

Now, for some ground rules before sharing the analogy widely.

Before you start assigning Dodgers players to actors, understand that Pacino was still excellent in The Godfather Part III. Shohei Ohtani, universally recognized as the greatest baseball player in the world, has not been.

Ohtani had batted under .200 in four straight postseason games. The Dodgers reportedly even considered benching him ahead of Game 3 because of his struggles and injuries.

A DODGERS-LESS WORLD SERIES WOULD HURT NOW, BUT HELP MLB LATER | BOBBY BURACK

But if the Dodgers don't somehow surge back from 0-3 and become just the second team in MLB history to overcome such a deficit in an LCS series, the Godfather analogy could hold up remarkably well.

The Godfather and The Godfather Part II are two of the greatest films ever made. The opinion here is that the original is the greatest movie ever and the sequel – which is also partly a prequel – is somewhere in the top 10, maybe the top five.

Part III isn't nearly as bad as some movie buffs sometimes portray it. However, it was undoubtedly a profound disappointment compared to the first two films.

For one, Coppola cast his daughter Sofia as Mary Corleone. It didn't work. The romance between Mary and her first cousin Vincent consumed too much screen time for how little it ultimately contributed to the trilogy's conclusion.

The absence of Tom Hagen is glaring, as is the loss of Sonny Corleone, whose death in the original film deprived the third installment of another defining character from the Corleone family.

In sum, The Godfather trilogy would be remembered even more favorably had there never been a third film. There's a reason some Godfather marathons conveniently end after Part II.

Likewise, if the Dodgers don't come back in this series, the 2026 team will be remembered as a stain on the legacy of the dynasty.

Still, The Godfather Part III had excuses.

The film was released 16 years after Part II. The principal cast had aged. Robert Duvall, who portrayed Hagen, did not return. And after nearly two decades, the first two films had been elevated to a standard that virtually no sequel could reasonably meet.

The 2026 Dodgers have no such excuses.

Their payroll exceeds that of the other three remaining teams combined. Los Angeles added Tarik Skubal and Kyle Tucker to a roster that was already considered one of the greatest ever assembled on paper.

Granted, the cast, like in the film, is aging. They are trying to recapture old magic. It's not working.

Nonetheless, we enjoyed the analogy. The Godfather Part III and the Dodgers' 2026 postseason are shaping up as two of the more memorable disappointments in their respective fields.

Even depressed Dodgers superfan and OutKick reporter Ian Miller appreciated Cowherd's comparison.

"There’s a case to be made that The Godfather Part 1 and Godfather Part 2 are two of the best movies ever made. Just like the 2024-2025 Dodgers are two of the best teams ever. If the price for that is getting pulled back in for the 2026 team, it was worth it," Miller said of Cowherd's analogy.

He did, however, add one important qualifier:

"As long as they don’t make Megalopolis next year, of course."

item.title: Democratic senator accuses Biden administration of 'completely' chickening out on Supreme Court reform
item.description: Sheldon Whitehouse said the Biden administration was "completely chicken" on Supreme Court reform, while Kamala Harris now pushes court expansion.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I., called out the Biden administration on Wednesday for a lack of action taken on the Supreme Court and said they were "completely chicken" on it.

The Lever's David Sirota asked Whitehouse about what "legitimate" resistance to the court might look like if a Democratic president believed the Supreme Court was "enabling an anti-democratic project."

"Well, I think it starts with truth telling and I think the chief executive of the United States has the proverbial bully, the bulliest of all pulpits, and should be prepared to make the argument about what has gone wrong with the courts. The Biden administration was highly reluctant to do that. They completely chickened out. Biden set up that lame committee commission on the Supreme Court and then squelched both Judge Gertner and Professor Tribe when they wanted to describe some of the actual problems at the court so that they couldn't even get that into the report," Whitehouse said.

LIBERAL JUSTICE HAMMERS SUPREME COURT FOR FAST-TRACKING EMERGENCY DOCKET CASES

He continued, "The Biden people didn't want to go there. They were completely chicken about all that. They wanted no part of that. And it — really wasn't until the very end, in his last speech after he and Harris had both lost that Biden seemed to have at least somewhat awakened to the fact that the Supreme Court had a real integrity problem."

FLASHBACK: DEM SENATOR EMBROILED IN CONFLICT OF INTEREST ROW TARGETED SCOTUS IN ETHICS CRUSADE

Nancy Gertner and Laurence Tribe served on former President Biden's Presidential Commission on the Supreme Court. Gertner and Tribe wrote an op-ed in The Washington Post in December 2021, calling for adding more justices to the court after the commission ultimately took no position on adding more justices.

DEMOCRATIC SENATOR CLAIMS GOP 'STOLE' TWO SCOTUS SEATS IN 2016, 2020, CALLS FOR EXPANSION

Gertner and Tribe were two of the 34 members of the commission, and wrote in The Washington Post, "We now believe that Congress must expand the size of the Supreme Court and do so as soon as possible. We did not come to this conclusion lightly."

Whitehouse has been a proponent of Supreme Court ethics legislation as he has argued that the Court has been captured by "right-wing billionaires and special interests."

GAVIN NEWSOM EXPRESSES 'OPENNESS' TO PACKING SCOTUS, CALLS ELECTORAL COLLEGE SYSTEM 'PERVERTED'

Former Vice President Kamala Harris called for expanding the Supreme Court during an interview on Wednesday, among other big institutional changes, which included Electoral College reform.

"The work that we can do about winning back the House and the Senate is going to be on a number of things. For example, I believe that we need to expand the Supreme Court. We need more justices on the Supreme Court so that we can have a court that actually reinforces the spirit and principles behind the Constitution of the United States," Harris told podcast host Keke Palmer on her "Baby, This is Keke Palmer" podcast. "I believe that we should be pushing for what is possible around changing the Electoral College. Right?"

HARRIS LABELED 'INSTITUTIONAL ARSONIST' FOR PLAN TO FUNDAMENTALLY TRANSFORM SCOTUS AND ELECTORAL COLLEGE

She also called for pursuing statehood for Washington, D.C., as well as Puerto Rico. Her comments come days after her 2024 vice presidential running mate, Gov. Tim Walz, warned of a reckoning among Democrats if the party fails to deliver on structural change and promises should they take back Congress and potentially the presidency in 2028.

"The odds of Democrats changing the composition of the Supreme Court through a constitutional amendment are near zero, while changing it via statutory legislation (such as expanding the number of seats or imposing term limits) would be extraordinarily difficult. It is a pipe dream. A fantasy. It’s nothing more than something to get their base excited about," Northwestern adjunct law professor Andrew Stoltmann told Fox News Digital in a statement.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

He continued, "A constitutional amendment requires a two-thirds vote in both the House of Representatives and the Senate, followed by ratification by three-fourths (38 of 50) of state legislatures. Given the deep divides, politically, this is almost impossible. It’s almost silly for Democrats to be arguing that this is a realistic possibility."

Biden's office did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Washington state's high school sports league puts onus for trans athlete controversy on state laws
item.description: The WIAA says Washington state law prevents it from banning males from girls' sports, even if members vote for change. Initiative 638 heads to voters.
item.content:encoded:
Washington state has been rocked in recent weeks by a controversy involving a male cross-country runner who switched from a boys’ team to a girls’ team mid-season. The controversy culminated in a protest Tuesday, when about a dozen female runners for Camas High School walked off the course, refusing to compete with their new male teammate.

The association governing Washington school sports says state law prevents it from implementing the proposed changes to its participation policy.

In a statement to OutKick, the Washington Interscholastic Activities Association (WIAA) said it cannot adopt a new policy to keep males out of girls’ sports, even if its members vote for a policy change, as it would be "in violation of Washington state law."

DAD BANNED FROM SCHOOL GROUNDS AFTER PROTESTING TRANS RUNNER COMPETING AGAINST HIS DAUGHTER

"In the last two years, through the association’s amendment process, three amendments have been proposed to alter the gender-identity participation policies. Those amendments did not meet the 60% threshold to pass. Nevertheless, even if the amendments had met the threshold and passed, the WIAA cannot implement a policy that is in violation of Washington state law and the amendments proposed would have violated state law. If state law changes, the WIAA Executive Board will revise policies as necessary to remain in compliance with state law," part of the WIAA’s statement read.

Washington voters are set to decide whether to change the rules next month.

Initiative 638, which would prohibit biological male students from competing in certain female-only school sports and require a healthcare provider's verification of biological sex, will be on the state ballot on Nov. 3.

Democrats currently hold majorities in both chambers of the state legislature and control the governor’s office. Democratic Gov. Bob Ferguson has expressed opposition to Initiative 638.

WHERE TOP DEMOCRAT SENATE CANDIDATES AND THEIR GOP OPPONENTS STAND ON TRANS ATHLETES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS

"Washingtonians should know that I-638 won’t create opportunities for girls, but it will force them into invasive sex verification exams in order to participate in sports," Ferguson said in a statement published Sept. 29 by the opposition campaign, No Hate in WA State.

The measure reached the ballot after lawmakers took no action on it during the 2026 session. Earlier this year, Democratic legislative leaders said they would leave the decision to voters.

The vote will come as the state grapples with multiple controversies involving males in girls’ sports, including the Camas cross-country runner and a separate incident involving a transgender wrestler who allegedly sexually assaulted a female athlete during a match last December, according to the female athlete’s lawsuit. Prosecutors declined to file criminal charges in that case.

In its statement to OutKick, the WIAA described itself as a membership-driven association whose members create its rules. It said its gender-identity participation policy has been in place since the 2007-08 school year and was adopted to align with Washington law.

"The WIAA is a membership-driven association. The membership creates the rules found in the WIAA Handbook. The gender-identity participation policies found in the WIAA Handbook at Rule 18.16.0 have been in place for 20 years, since the 2007-08 school year. The rules were passed to align with Washington state law. The WIAA remains committed to following Washington state law … which permits student-athletes to participate in sports consistent with the gender with which they identify," the statement read.

"WIAA Handbook 18.16.0 states that school personnel will work collaboratively with the student to determine eligibility, however, a timeline for switching teams is not designated. WIAA Handbook 17.11 establishes practice regulations, outlining the minimum number of practice requirements. WIAA Handbook 18.2.1 demonstrates that student’s must be deemed eligible by the respective sport’s 50% date in order to be eligible to participate in postseason competition.

"The WIAA Handbook provides the framework for schools, leagues, and WIAA Districts to operate events throughout the year. The WIAA Office does not manage day-to-day league and WIAA District events and instead is tasked with running WIAA State Tournaments. For example, the WIAA Office establishes signage policies for WIAA State events, but not league or WIAA District contests. Once again, the WIAA is a membership-driven association."

After the U.S. Supreme Court upheld other states’ laws restricting transgender athletes’ participation in girls’ and women’s sports in landmark rulings in June, Washington’s Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction (OSPI) said the decisions did not change Washington law. The agency said Superintendent Chris Reykdal would continue enforcing state law allowing students to compete consistent with their gender identity.

"Today’s decision reinforces Washington state’s ability to adopt and implement our own laws in alignment with our values," Reykdal said in the June 30 statement.

The distinction matters for families seeking a different policy: a ruling allowing states to restrict participation does not itself enact such a restriction in Washington.

Initiative 638 would require school districts and covered athletic associations to prohibit students it defines as biologically male from competing with or against female students in certain competitions intended for female students only. It would apply to individual and team events.

Students entering those competitions would have to provide a signed statement from a personal healthcare provider verifying biological sex through reproductive anatomy, genetic makeup or naturally produced testosterone levels.

Backers, led by Let’s Go Washington, say the measure would preserve fair competition and opportunities for girls. They argue that transgender students would retain opportunities to participate in sports in categories corresponding to their sex.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Opponents say the measure would exclude transgender girls and create new medical and privacy burdens for girls seeking to play school sports.

Supporters dispute Ferguson’s characterization of the verification requirement. Let’s Go Washington says the measure does not mandate genital examinations and that verification could occur through the existing sports-physical process.

The political decision to leave the initiative for voters was clear months before the Camas protest.

In January, Senate Majority Leader Jamie Pedersen and House Speaker Laurie Jinkins said they did not plan to hold hearings on the sports initiative and a separate parental-rights measure, according to the Washington State Standard.

"I’m certain that we will not be passing either of those initiatives," Pedersen said, per the Washington State Standard. "They’ll be up to the voters to decide."

item.title: Rep Andy Harris threatens to have student journalist prosecuted for recording press conference
item.description: University of Maryland's journalism school defended Cat Murphy after GOP Rep. Andy Harris wrongly claimed her recording violated Maryland consent law.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Andy Harris, R-Md., incorrectly insisted that a University of Maryland student journalist was violating state law when she recorded him at a news conference, threatening to refer her to prosecutors during a heated exchange after a debate Tuesday.

Speaking in a crowded hallway after an October 13 debate with Democratic challenger Dan Schwartz, Harris demanded that University of Maryland student journalist Cat Murphy stop recording the news conference, arguing that Maryland's two-party consent law required his permission. He was annoyed that she defended a reporter from the Baltimore Banner, who had irked him with a "silly" question about why he participated in the debate. 

"You do not have my permission to record. If you record, we will refer you to the prosecutor," Harris told Murphy, who responded that other journalists were already recording the news conference.

PRESS FREEDOM GROUPS THAT BLASTED TRUMP TURN FIRE ON DEM GOVERNOR OVER ALLEGED MEDIA RETALIATION

"But you are not allowed to. We are in a two-party state, you are not allowed to," an agitated Harris said while pointing in the student’s face.

The student asked why she, specifically, wasn’t allowed to record and Harris continued to grow frustrated.

"Because I refuse to give you permission to record," Harris said. "Do you know the law?"

The student attempted to have a different journalist hold her recording device, and a separate reporter tried to explain to Harris that the interview was occurring in a public forum.

"I’m a legislator… I actually know the law well," Harris insisted.

VIDEO SHOWS MAINE WIRE REPORTER NEARLY BEING RUN OVER BY CAR AFTER CONFRONTATION

Murphy then tried to question Harris, who represents Maryland's 1st Congressional District, about the war in Iran.

"You’re going to have to take her camera," Harris said to someone in the room. "She is violating the law. In fact, get an officer in here. She’s violating the law on two-party recording. We need an officer."

Other reporters repeatedly told Harris they were "in public," but he responded that it "makes no difference whatsoever."

LAWMAKER’S STUNNED FACE AND OTHER VIRAL MOMENTS CAP ROUGH WEEK FOR POLITICAL CLASS

Harris continued to insist that Murphy needed his permission to record before ending the news conference and walking away.

"She’s ruining all your chances to get an answer about anything. See y’all," he said while exiting. "Thank her profusely."

In Maryland, the consent requirement only applies to "private conversation," according to the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press (RCFP). Footage of the incident quickly went viral, and Harris was widely mocked for botching the law.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The University of Maryland's Philip Merrill College of Journalism, where Murphy is a student, defended her actions in a statement.

"Cat Murphy is a master's student at the University of Maryland, credentialed as a reporter for our Capital News Service and doing the job we teach our students to do. Cat recorded openly in a public space alongside other news outlets, and that is her legal right," Dean Rafael Lorente said in a statement. "I'm proud of how she handled herself in a difficult situation."

Harris’ office did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Fox News Digital.

Merrill College of Journalism did not immediately respond when asked for comment from Murphy.

Murphy told CNN that Harris had suggested during the debate that the war in Iran could have gone "smoother," and she was seeking clarification.

The exchange also drew reactions from journalists and other social media users.

Harris is the only Republican in Maryland's congressional delegation.

item.title: Comedian Bert Kreischer compares perfect burger to great sex: 'Doesn't need to be fancy'
item.description: Comedian Bert Kreischer shares his burger preference, his smash burger obsession and why Guy Fieri's Carnival cruise burger bar serves the best burger he's ever had.
item.content:encoded:
Comedian Bert Kreischer knows a thing or two about burgers, and his recipe for the perfect one is surprisingly simple — even if his description is anything but family-friendly.

"A good burger is like great sex. It doesn't need to be fancy," Kreischer said in an interview ahead of his appearance as host of the Burger Bash at Thursday night's New York City Wine & Food Festival.

For Kreischer, the ideal burger doesn't require exotic ingredients or elaborate toppings. He prefers the classics: a buttery, toasted brioche bun, American cheese and traditional fixings.

WAHLBURGERS CHEF PAUL WAHLBERG SHARES SIMPLE RULES FOR GRILLING PERFECT MEMORIAL DAY BURGER

"I've got to be in a mood to have a raspberry jam and goat cheese on a burger," he said.

The comedian's passion for burgers goes well beyond punchlines.

On his cooking show, "Something's Burning," Kreischer became so proficient at making smash burgers that he found himself eating them around the clock.

"I got so good at making smash burgers that I went through a smash burger phase where I was having them for breakfast, lunch and dinner," he recalled.

STOP MAKING A COMMON BURGER MISTAKE, CHEF WARNS: 'ONE OF THE WORST THINGS YOU CAN DO'

Eventually, Kreischer said, he had to stop making them so frequently.

But one burger still holds a special place in his heart: the one served at Guy Fieri's burger bar aboard Carnival cruise ships.

"The best thing Guy Fieri has ever done in his life is the f------ Guy Fieri burger bar on the cruise ships," Kreischer said. "That is the best burger you'll ever have."

He particularly appreciates the generous portions, the option to double up on patties and cheese, and the freedom to customize his burger with whatever toppings he wants.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Kreischer, who is preparing to host his own Fully Loaded at Sea comedy cruise featuring a live taping of "Something's Burning," said he'd happily spend an afternoon making burgers behind the counter if the ship had a Guy Fieri burger bar.

For now, his attention is on Burger Bash, where some of the country's top burger makers will compete for bragging rights.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Although Kreischer has no shortage of opinions about what makes a winning burger, he's relieved that his role is to host rather than judge, as he did earlier this year at the South Beach Wine & Food Festival.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Yeah, it's so much better than judging it," he said.

For Kreischer, the best burgers aren't necessarily the most adventurous. Sometimes, a perfectly cooked patty, melted American cheese and a toasted bun are all it takes.

item.title: Ilhan Omar's husband snaps over rumors she fled US after federal immigration fraud raid
item.description: Tim Mynett was spotted at the couple's D.C. home as HSI's fraud investigation into Ilhan Omar's immigration paperwork intensifies with new subpoenas.
item.content:encoded:
While Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., has not been seen publicly since federal agents raided her Washington, D.C., residence on Monday, her political consultant husband was once again spotted emerging from their shared rental home this week.

Tim Mynett was seen Wednesday stepping out in the neighborhood to walk their Golden Labrador Retriever dog Teddy, a second time later that same day to take out the trash and a third time to walk out his wife's staffer.

"There are rumors that the congresswoman left the country, is that true?" Mynett was asked while on an evening walk with Teddy.

"You guys are annoying the hell out of all the neighbors around here, man," he told Fox News Digital when approached about the developments this week, including President Donald Trump weighing in on the saga.

One of Omar's congressional staffers was captured the same day bringing into the couple's home two large bags from fast food chain Burger King. Security escorted her to the door and staked out in front of the house after she entered with the meal.

ILHAN OMAR’S EMBATTLED HUSBAND APPEARS AT SCENE OF HSI RAID IN MIDST OF CRIMINAL FRAUD INVESTIGATION

Rumors swirled that Omar fled from the country following the raid carried out by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) as part of a criminal fraud investigation looking into the Somali-born congresswoman’s immigration paperwork, as first reported by Fox News Digital.

Omar’s cellphone and passport were reportedly seized by federal authorities during the search.

The congresswoman's staff helped to get her birth year adjusted from 1981 to 1982 in the Minnesota Legislative Reference Library, according to reporters. Omar gained citizenship automatically through her father’s naturalization since she was reportedly 17 years old at the time. If Omar was born in 1981, she would have been 18 years old, meaning the validity of her citizenship could be threatened because she was no longer a minor.

The altered birthdate was published during her entire time serving in Minnesota’s House and for months into her time serving in Congress.

When asked about the federal investigation earlier this week, Mynett told Fox News Digital he has "no concerns" about what federal authorities will find on his wife while investigating her immigration pathway.

"My wife came here when she was 12 years old as a child war refugee," Mynett said. "No concerns."

His comments to Fox News Digital come after Omar’s relatives were reportedly issued subpoenas as part of HSI’s investigation into the congresswoman's immigration paperwork. At least two of Omar's relatives were subpoenaed, one of which is reportedly Omar’s sister, Sahra Noor.

OMAR FACES MOUNTING SCRUTINY AFTER FRAUD RINGLEADER SENTENCED TO 41 YEARS

Scrutiny of Omar's finances intensified after her 2024 congressional financial disclosure listed business interests associated with Mynett valued between $6 million and $30 million. Omar's office subsequently said the figures were incorrect and amended the filing.

The largest change in the documents was from Mynett’s assets. His reported ownership interests in both his winery and venture capital advisory firm, which were previously valued in the millions of dollars, are listed with no value now.

In Omar’s 2024 financial disclosure records, Mynett’s share in his winery was valued between $1 million and $5 million, and his share at the venture capital advisory firm was valued between $5 million and $25 million. Now, his equity interests are both listed at $0.

Omar's office previously told Fox News Digital that Mynett has partners in both businesses and said the earlier disclosure mistakenly reflected the businesses' total equity rather than his ownership interest. item.title: College Football Playoff expanding to 24 teams in 2027, with more games coming to campuses across the country
item.description: ESPN is set to finalize a deal Thursday to broadcast the expanded 24-team College Football Playoff, featuring 19 at-large bids and campus games.
item.content:encoded:
The College Football Playoff is doubling up.

After what will be just three years of having a 12-team CFB Playoff, the field is being expanded to 24 teams beginning in 2027.

Signs have long been pointing to an expansion, but now the final piece of the puzzle has all but fallen into place with ESPN reportedly jumping on board; this drastic change to the sport is taking shape in a hurry.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Sources have confirmed with OutKick's Trey Wallace that a meeting between representatives from ESPN and the College Football Playoff will take place on Thursday, in which the financial aspects of the deal will be presented between the two. It is expected that the deal will be agreed upon, which will result in ESPN purchasing the additional games that come with the expanded tournament. ESPN's current deal to broadcast the College Football Playoff runs through 2031.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

With the addition of Playoff games, it is safe to assume that 2026 will be the final year we see conference championship games played across Power Four and Group of Six conferences. Additionally, fewer bowl games will take place beginning in 2027.

Sources also confirmed with Wallace that the 24-team Playoff bracket will feature 19 at-large bids, with one auto bid going to each of the Power Four conferences and the fifth and final auto bid going to a Group of Six team.

One of the more intriguing wrinkles of the expanded Playoff is that the first two rounds of the postseason tournament will, according to sources, be played on campuses.

As noted by Wallace in early October, the SEC and Big Ten, the two most powerful conferences in the sport, were the final two entities to come to a decision on the expansion. ESPN owns the television rights to the SEC, while the Big Ten is under contract with FOX, which could make for an interesting dynamic behind the scenes.

Aside from this move likely signaling the end of conference title games, it could signal a new era in the Big Ten with teams having to commit to more difficult non-conference games. Sources tell Wallace that Big Ten teams could be mandated to add a Power Four opponent to the calendar.

The SEC made a proactive move ahead of this current college football season by moving to a nine-game conference schedule.

Over the hump and safely into a big Thursday — which, during the fall, is basically the start of the weekend.

Let's roll.

Though Mamdani said he was reviewing the circumstances of the shooting, he had no plans to remove Tisch.

"Jessica Tisch is the police commissioner. I have no plans to change that," Mamdani told reporters Tuesday.

MAMDANI CALLS ICE A 'ROGUE' AGENCY AFTER NYC SHOOTING, CLAIMS AGENTS VIEW LAW AS 'MERELY A SUGGESTION'

"They were p----- about what she did on social media and her public rhetoric on NYPD," one source told the New York Post. "City Hall was like, ‘What the f--- are you doing!’"

"She is throwing her own fireball rhetoric to rally the folks," another source added. "But instigating doesn’t help."

According to the New York Post, these sources described Chevalier as a known "potential liability" for the Mamdani administration for a while and were surprised as to how soon she became a problem.

MAMDANI-BACKED SOCIALIST WITH HISTORY OF ANTI-AMERICAN RHETORIC WINS VICIOUS DEM PRIMARY RACE

MAMDANI DEMANDS TRUMP RELEASE ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT SHOT BY ICE AGENT AS PROTESTS ERUPT IN THE BRONX

"The Police Commissioner was giving a factual update on the incident, and we always provide criminal history in incident updates, if we have it. It’s also one of the first questions that every media outlet asks the NYPD," the statement read.

New York State Republican Party Director of Communications David Laska denounced the Democratic Party as a whole for leaving Mamdani as a voice of reason.

"Zohran Mamdani helped create this monster with years of anti-American, antisemitic rhetoric, and now it's eating him alive. History reminds us that even Robespierre was guillotined in the end," Laska told Fox News Digital.

item.title: Fort Hood survivors praise Trump for scrapping Hasan execution livestream: ‘We’re not barbaric’
item.description: Alonzo Lunsford, shot seven times by Nidal Hasan, called Trump's decision to cancel the firing squad livestream a "positive move" for the nation.
item.content:encoded:
Survivors of the 2009 Fort Hood massacre praised President Donald Trump's decision not to livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan, after warning that broadcasting his death could turn the execution into a spectacle and hand terrorist groups a propaganda tool.

Hasan is still set to be executed by firing squad on Dec. 3, 2026, and Trump said the immediate families of his victims will be permitted to witness the execution in person. But it will no longer be broadcast to the general public as previously announced by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth.

Alonzo Lunsford, who was shot seven times by Hasan during the attack nearly 17 years ago, told Fox News Digital that Trump's decision is a "positive move."

"It proves that we are a better people, a better nation, and that we're not barbaric," Lunsford said in immediate reaction to the walk-back by Trump on Thursday. "We don't glorify such actions."

VETERAN SHOT 7 TIMES IN FORT HOOD MASSACRE HAS A WARNING FOR AMERICANS PLANNING TO WATCH EXECUTION

Lunsford said he supports Hasan's death sentence and execution by firing squad but drew a line at broadcasting it to the public.

"For it to be made a spectacle for everyone to witness how they're gonna do a tailgate or, 'Hey, we're gonna have a cookout and we're gonna watch this man be put to death.' No, it's not about that," Lunsford said. "It's not a spectacle. It's not a pay-per-view event or a WWE wrestling match or even a boxing match."

He also warned that footage of Hasan's execution could be seized upon by terrorist organizations.

"You don't want that to be used as a tool for ISIS or al-Qaeda to recruit and say, 'Hey, this is what happens to you if you do this against the infidel,'" Lunsford said.

Julia Wilson was a civilian employee at Fort Hood when Hasan went on his rampage. She was nine months pregnant during the attack, which was carried out on her due date.

FORT HOOD SHOOTER SHOULD BE EXECUTED '13 TIMES OVER' — BUT NOT ON LIVE STREAM, SURVIVOR SAYS

She was slammed against a wall amid the chaos of the shooting and has said that it was only by the grace of God that she and her then-unborn son survived.

Wilson was already against the livestreaming of Hasan's execution because she didn't want others to be traumatized like she was during the deadly attack.

"I'm ecstatic about that," she told Fox News Digital, reacting to the news that the plan to livestream the event would not proceed.

"I'm worried about other people's mental health," she continued. "I don't think the government… really put a lot of thought into how this was going to go down and how it was going to transpire until today."

"I don't think they really thought about how this may affect people," said Wilson. "Seeing something like that affects your mental health. I don't care who you are. I don't care what you've seen. Seeing someone murdered in front of you or killed in front of you affects your mental health, whether they deserve it or not."

Wilson also worried that if the livestream had proceeded, it would exist online forever, and that children might discover it while searching the web. "Once it's on out there, it's out there," she said.

Trump said Wednesday that he believed publicly broadcasting Hasan's death could have served as a deterrent, but ultimately sided with those who opposed making the execution available for anyone to watch.

"I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan but, many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

"He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed," Trump continued. "That said, the execution may be viewed in person by the immediate families of the victims, if they so choose. They deserve to witness JUSTICE!"

Lunsford pointed to warnings surrounding Hasan before the shooting and criticized the Army's handling of the future attacker before he was transferred from Walter Reed to Fort Hood.

"We knew this guy had issues," Lunsford said. "If you are privy to the ticking time bomb report, you will see what he was talking about. This guy had issues and they just passed the buck and moved him from Walter Reed to Fort Hood."

Lunsford wondered what might have happened had Hasan deployed overseas before carrying out an attack.

"Suppose he would have did the deed once he got in country on a FOB, a forward operating base," he said. "Imagine how many American lives would have been lost then."

For Lunsford, allowing victims to witness Hasan's execution remains important even without a public broadcast.

"It's gonna be a traumatic thing for, at least for the families of the fallen," he said. "They'll be able to close the chapter and hopefully close the book."

Lunsford said survivors will continue to live with reminders of the attack long after Hasan is gone.

"Every day we get up, we come to the VA hospital or we have to take our meds in the morning or we get ready to do something that we normally would have been doing prior to 5 November '09 that we're no longer able to do now, that's a constant reminder," he said.

"I am no longer a victim of his," Lunsford added. "I'm a survivor."

item.content:encoded:
Welcome to a Thursday in the middle of October. Or I should say, welcome to the latest edition of True Romance. Today is all about pushing back on the notion that romance has been defeated and it no longer exists.

For those buying in on that, and I'm sure for some it's the case, I present to you several examples that, despite a possible downward trend overall, there are those making it work. If nothing else, there's hope.

We have a full slate from the smooth athlete to influencer DM that landed to couple that pole dance together and even a couple of actors who covered their workplace in romance. Light a candle, relax and let’s get into it.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Long before the lucky pregame butt squeezes or the messages written on the back of Haley Cavinder's pants or even taking the heat for Jake Ferguson's bad game, there was the classic shooter taking his shot.

The Dallas Cowboys tight end slid into the former college athlete and influencer's DMs with a line that ended up working and anyone can use.

Haley said on an episode of People's WAG World, "He just DMed me and asked how my golf game was."

And there's this idea floating out there that you can't meet people. Firing off a wild DM usually doesn’t work. A "How's your golf game" is smooth. The two hit it off, and now they're married, with a story to tell their grandkids one day.

Grandpa was in the NFL and grandma used to dance on TikTok. They met after he sent her a message on social media. A love story as old as time.

"I don’t like to get high or too low when it comes to that stuff. I wasn’t looking for anything, and I don’t know if Ferg was at that time either," she continued.

"But then we spent 10 days together straight, and he’s just a good, down-to-earth human being."

If you're having trouble finding someone, maybe you're just looking in the wrong places and sending DMs that aren't landing. There is hope. Fire off one about golf to a TikToker and see what ends up playing out.

JOE BURROW'S GIRLFRIEND SHARES CHEATING HOT TAKE, WOMAN'S SISTER HOOKED UP WITH HER DATE & REGAINING THE SPARK

Before we move on, let's find out the results of the poll from last week. The "Do you go through with the wedding if your husband-to-be calls you your sister's name at the altar?" one.

In a stunner, given that the woman who this happened to did go through with the wedding, an overwhelming 72.5% said no, you leave that jerk at the altar. An unforgiving bunch of hopeless romantics, I suppose.

Go follow True Romance on Twitter and Facebook and keep sending your emails here: sean.joseph@outkick.com (anonymously if you prefer).

I bet, had that couple been pole dancing together, the husband-to-be wouldn’t have said the name of the bride's sister at the altar. Because if you didn’t already know, couples who pole dance together are weirdos.

Let me finish. Weirdos who "strengthen their bonds and keep the spark alive." Take it from Los Angeles newlyweds Misha and Sam who, if they need pole dancing or anything as newlyweds to keep the spark alive, might be doomed.

But that will be something they'll never be confronted with as long as they keep hopping on the pole together. And that's what we're here to focus on. The positive aspects of what these two are doing.

Their first dance featured "saucy flips and splits on the polished pole," according to the NY Post. It turns out hitting the pole can be done in front of others. That's an interesting twist to this that I didn’t see coming.

I was thinking this was more of an in the privacy of your own home activity. But why not something for everyone? Who needs movie nights or long walks when you have this and all of its options?

"There’s a lot of stigma around pole dancing, some people might think, ‘Oh, that’s just for strippers,’" Misha told The Post.

"Yes, it has sensual roots. But there’s so much athleticism that go into it. It’s a lot harder than it looks. We love it."

Sam, who is the one who suggested they get into pole dancing, said, "A lot of people think pole is just for women. It’s strange for them to see a guy do it, especially with his [female] partner. I just don’t feed into the negativity."

He added, "There are times I have to hold all of Misha’s weight while we’re doing a move, or she may have to position herself in a certain way to accommodate me. It’s like a metaphor for marriage."

There really is something out there for everyone. If you're willing to take a chance, you could be one of those who finds the person you want to pole dance with for the rest of your life. That's a lovely thought, isn't it?

If you think about it, pole dancing together really is just a metaphor for marriage.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Follow True Romance on Twitter and Facebook.

As much as I'd like to believe that couples pole dancing will work for people, and I'm sure it will for some, I can tell you a relationship built on having sex all over the set you're working on does work.

At least it has for Keri Russell and Matthew Rhys. They've been together since late 2013 after starting their relationship while working on the series "The Americans".

We now know that when they weren't filming they were busy on set having sex in their disguises. Why do we know that? Well, because it's 2026 and everyone tells everybody else everything.

Which reminds me, I'll have to tell the story sometime of a graveyard at night and the back of a Nissan Pathfinder. Anyway, back to Keri and Matthew making a mess of their workplace.

"We were falling in love and staying up all night and having sex all the time and just wearing disguises, like, I’m f---ing [in] crazy wigs and wearing pearls," Russell said during a podcast appearance, reports Entertainment Weekly.

"When have you ever worn pearls and [been] f---ing in trailers and f---ing everywhere. I mean, it was insanity. It was so fun and sneaky, and sexy, and so good."

If that doesn’t say true romance, I don't know what does. Congratulations to the happy couple for both their extracurricular activity on the set and for extending hope for others. Well done.

We've done a ton of these, and I don’t know that we've come across a more important question. She puts on her sexy underwear and he does what?

If you were expecting a lot of effort here, you're going to be disappointed by the folks weighing in on Reddit, although something tells me that won't be a first.

Sure, there are those who put in some work, but go ahead and set your expectations appropriately. Not that slipping on special underwear is a heavy lift.

Some guys do that too. A blown out waistband could ruin the mood. On the other hand, a lovely Borat-style mankini could get the evening going.

It’s called The Girl of My Best Friend. Unlike the guy in the column, the guy in the song had the good sense to keep his feelings to himself and just pine away for her. Hope this song is named Song of the Week. All the best.

Discovering that your identity has been stolen can leave you feeling angry, frightened and unsure where to begin. Maybe someone drained your bank account, opened a credit card in your name or filed a fraudulent tax return using your Social Security number. Whatever happened, your next steps can help limit the damage.

The first 24 hours are especially important because identity thieves may continue using your information until you secure your accounts. Fortunately, you can take several steps right away to protect yourself and begin recovering.

IDENTITY RESTORATION: WHAT TO DO AFTER IDENTITY THEFT

Identity theft can quickly spread beyond the account where you first discovered the problem. Someone who gains access to your email, for example, might use it to reset passwords for your banking, shopping or other accounts. That's why acting quickly can make a difference.

However, you don't have to solve everything in one day. Identity theft recovery can take weeks or even months, depending on the circumstances. Your immediate goal is to stop additional fraud, protect your information and create a record of what happened.

The following checklist breaks the process into manageable steps. The time frames are guidelines, so prioritize active fraud and compromised accounts rather than waiting for a particular hour.

Start with the accounts most likely to expose your money or personal information.

Important: If money has been stolen, report it to your financial institution immediately. Federal protections and reporting deadlines vary by account and transaction type.

Next, make it harder for criminals to open additional accounts using your personal information.

You can freeze your credit even if you expect to apply for a loan or credit card soon. Simply lift the freeze temporarily when necessary.

Creating an official record can help you dispute fraudulent accounts and recover your identity.

An FTC identity theft report can help you exercise certain rights under federal law, including requesting that credit bureaus block fraudulent information. However, you generally do not need to file an FTC report before notifying a bank about unauthorized transactions.

A SCAMMER HAS YOUR NAME, PHONE NUMBER AND ADDRESS. WHAT CAN THEY ACTUALLY DO?

Identity thieves sometimes try to use stolen information across multiple services.

Hours 16 to 24: Document everything

Once you've addressed the most urgent threats, organize your recovery efforts.

Even when you're moving quickly, certain mistakes can create additional problems.

9 WARNING SIGNS OF IDENTITY THEFT YOU SHOULD NEVER IGNORE

Some recovery tasks will continue beyond the first day, including disputing fraudulent accounts, correcting credit reports and following up with creditors. However, report unauthorized financial transactions immediately. Federal protections and reporting deadlines vary depending on the type of account and transaction. Your initial priority is to stop additional fraud and secure your information.

Recovering from identity theft often involves contacting multiple financial institutions, disputing fraudulent charges and keeping track of important paperwork. An identity theft protection service may help simplify the process by offering recovery assistance, ongoing monitoring and guidance when suspicious activity appears.

Keep in mind that no identity theft protection service can prevent every type of fraud or guarantee that stolen money will be recovered. You can also take important steps for free, including freezing your credit, placing fraud alerts and reporting identity theft at IdentityTheft.gov.

Many people go through this first-24-hours checklist not for themselves, but for an aging parent, a spouse or another family member. If you're the one helping, the same steps apply. Start by securing compromised accounts, freezing credit, reporting fraud and documenting what happened. Keep in mind that you may need permission or legal authorization to speak with financial institutions on someone else's behalf.

Patience is important, too. Identity theft can be frightening, especially for someone who isn't comfortable managing financial accounts online. Helping them make phone calls, organize paperwork and track important deadlines can make the recovery process easier.

Once the first 24 hours are behind you, continue working through your checklist. Dispute fraudulent charges and accounts, follow up on your identity theft report and request that fraudulent information be removed from your credit reports. Keep monitoring your financial accounts for suspicious activity, since criminals may attempt additional fraud using stolen information.

Recovery timelines vary depending on the type and extent of the theft. Some problems can be resolved quickly, while more complicated cases may take months.

Consider asking a trusted family member or close friend to help you stay organized. Having someone review documents, take notes or track deadlines can help prevent important details from slipping through the cracks.

The most important thing is to stay focused on what you can control. Secure your accounts, report suspicious activity promptly and follow through on unresolved disputes. You may not fix everything in the first 24 hours, but taking these steps can help limit further damage and put you on the path to recovery.

When someone steals your identity, it's easy to feel like you've lost control of your financial life. I've seen how quickly one compromised account can lead to bigger problems, especially when criminals get access to email or other personal information. My advice is to focus on what you can control right away. Contact your bank, secure your most important accounts and freeze your credit with all three bureaus. Then report the theft and keep a record of every conversation. You don't need to pay a company to take these initial steps. I also recommend keeping an eye on your accounts long after the first day. Identity thieves may try to use stolen information again, even after you've addressed the original problem. A little extra attention now can help you catch suspicious activity before it causes more damage.
